title: Radiators and Postcards
premise: Isandro Sandoval has spent thirty years translating other people's words while letting his mother tongue, Kavreni, erode into a handful of borrowed phrases he uses like talismans. When Marta Ilves, the last fluent speaker of Kavreni, summons him as her final student, he resists—teaching the language to one person cannot save it, and learning it means remembering the neighborhood, and the brother, he left behind. As the city reroutes the last bus line through the old district, Isandro and Marta rebuild a vocabulary and, with it, a found family of misfits who begin recording what they can. When Marta dies mid-lesson, Isandro must decide whether a language that lives in one grieving throat is still a language at all; he answers by delivering her eulogy in Kavreni at her funeral, out loud, imperfect, before the bus makes its final run.
about_author: Quentin Okonkwo is the pen name of a former court interpreter who grew up between three languages and claims to dream in none of them. Radiators and Postcards is their second novel, written in the margins of a decade spent translating other people's testimony.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Isandro, working a soulless corporate translation job, deflects a colleague's friendly overtures with his practiced smile. At night he counts the Kavreni words he can still remember—eleven, down from thousands. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the quiet shame of a man fluent in everyone's language but his own.

chapters.title: A Letter in a Dying Alphabet
chapters.summary: A handwritten letter arrives in Kavreni, addressed to 'the Sandoval boy who still owes a word.' Isandro can read only fragments. His neighbor Odile, a retired postmistress, helps him decipher the return address: a hospital in the old neighborhood. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Eleven Words
chapters.summary: Isandro catalogs his surviving vocabulary in a notebook: words for radiator, for snowmelt, for a particular goodbye. Each word drags up a memory of his brother Teo, who stayed in the neighborhood and stopped writing. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: inventory as elegy.

chapters.title: The Last Bus Route
chapters.summary: City notices announce the 47 bus—the only line still serving the old district—will be rerouted in three months. Isandro realizes his window to return is literally closing. He does not buy a ticket. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: paralysis dressed up as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Marta Ilves Speaks to No One
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters begin: Marta, 89, in her hospital room, speaking Kavreni to the radiator because no one else can hear it. A young nurse records her secretly, thinking it's gibberish, until a linguist confirms the language has one speaker left. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: loneliness as a form of loyalty.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Isandro visits Marta, expecting to decline politely. She refuses his smile, assigns him homework, and tells him his mother once promised her a student. He leaves without agreeing, but takes the homework. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: being seen against his will.

chapters.title: Homework
chapters.summary: Isandro completes Marta's exercises on his kitchen floor, relearning numbers and seasons. Odile starts sitting with him, learning alongside, though she has no claim to the language. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the terrifying warmth of company.

chapters.title: What Teo Kept
chapters.summary: Isandro learns Teo died two years ago; Marta was with him at the end. A shoebox of Teo's belongings—postcards Isandro never sent—arrives via Marta. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: grief arriving late, in someone else's handwriting.

chapters.title: The Nurse's Recordings
chapters.summary: The nurse, Priya, confesses she recorded Marta and offers the tapes. Isandro is furious—consent, ownership, theft—until he hears Marta singing a lullaby his mother sang. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: anger and gratitude occupying the same breath.

chapters.title: Radiator
chapters.summary: Marta teaches the word for radiator—the sound a room makes when it loves you back. She reveals she chose Isandro not for his fluency but because he still says thank you in Kavreni without noticing. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: a teacher's fierce, unsentimental hope.

chapters.title: Odile's Claim
chapters.summary: Odile asks, hurt, why she can't be a real student too. Isandro, cruel in his grief, says the language isn't hers. Odile stops coming. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under the pressure of authenticity.

chapters.title: Postcards, Unsent
chapters.summary: Isandro reads Teo's postcards—thirty years of them, addressed but never mailed, describing a brother's life in a language Isandro is only now relearning. The last one says: 'Tell Marta I kept it.' POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the discovery that Teo never let go.

chapters.title: The Reroute Advances
chapters.summary: Demolition begins on the old district; the hospital will be relocated. Marta refuses transfer, insisting she'll die in a room with a working radiator. Isandro starts visiting daily. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: urgency compressing love into grammar drills.

chapters.title: Words That Don't Translate
chapters.summary: Marta teaches the untranslatables: a word for grief that is also gratitude, a word for a door left open on purpose. Isandro begins dreaming in Kavreni. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the language returning like blood to a numb limb.

chapters.title: The Apology
chapters.summary: Isandro goes to Odile's flat with a Kavreni apology he wrote himself, mistakes and all. She can't understand it but understands it anyway. She returns, bringing her granddaughter, who starts recording lessons properly, with consent. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: repair without erasure.

chapters.title: The Archive Question
chapters.summary: A university linguist offers to archive Marta's speech—thousands of hours, preserved forever. Marta asks Isandro whether a language in a hard drive is alive. He cannot answer. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: the ethics of saving versus keeping.

chapters.title: Snowmelt
chapters.summary: Marta's health fails; lessons move to her bedside. She teaches the word for snowmelt—the season when the frozen river lets go. She makes Isandro promise to say the goodbye properly, out loud, when the time comes. He promises before he knows what it costs. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: a promise made in the present tense of dread.

chapters.title: The Last Full Lesson
chapters.summary: Marta, lucid one final morning, conducts a complete lesson: the whole surviving grammar of Kavreni in four hours, Priya recording, Odile's granddaughter transcribing. Marta ends by saying the goodbye word to each of them individually. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: ceremony improvised from almost nothing.

chapters.title: Silence in the Room with the Radiator
chapters.summary: Marta dies on a Tuesday, mid-homework, the radiator ticking. Isandro sits with her for hours, speaking Kavreni aloud to the room because it is the only way to keep breathing. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: grief that is also fluency, finally.

chapters.title: The Eulogy
chapters.summary: At the funeral, Isandro abandons the prepared English remarks and delivers the eulogy in Kavreni—imperfect, halting, out loud, in front of everyone. Priya plays Marta's lullaby afterward. Odile holds his hand. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the climax—truth spoken over loyalty to invisibility.

chapters.title: The Final Run of the 47
chapters.summary: On the last day of the bus route, Isandro, Odile, Priya, and the granddaughter ride it end to end, reading Teo's postcards aloud and translating them into Kavreni as a small act of resurrection. Strangers listen. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: mourning converted into transmission.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words, Returned
chapters.summary: A year later: Isandro teaches a Saturday class of seven students in a community room with a loud radiator; the archive exists, but so does the classroom. He still has the smile that ends conversations, but he no longer needs it. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: a language alive in imperfect, willing mouths.
